log.action: Draw my sword and charge toward the sounds of fighting.

You know the economy of that restraint in your marrow: dead men fetch nothing at market.Then the big one turns.He is broad as a barn door, his left eye milky-white, a brand burned into his jaw in the shape of a crescent and chain. The brand of Valerius's pit operation. You know that mark. You bore a collar above it for two years."Well," Void Ironside says, and his ruined mouth pulls into something that was never a smile. "The wolf wandered back to the fold all on his own."Three of the pack spread to flank you. Void steps forward alone, drawing a hand-axe that is notched from long use.🔊………

Steel clears leather with a sound like a warning, and your legs are already driving you south along the wagon ruts before conscious thought catches up. The scene that opens before you is efficient carnage. A merchant caravan, three wagons heavy with cloth and salted goods, sits jackknifed across the road, one horse dead in its traces, another screaming with an arrow in its flank. Four men in mismatched leather armor move between the wagons with professional ease, clubbing down the merchant's guards rather than killing them. Slavers. You know the economy of that restraint in your marrow: dead men fetch nothing at market.

Then the big one turns.

He is broad as a barn door, his left eye milky-white, a brand burned into his jaw in the shape of a crescent and chain. The brand of Valerius's pit operation. You know that mark. You bore a collar above it for two years.

[SAY:Void Ironside]"Well," Void Ironside says, and his ruined mouth pulls into something that was never a smile. "The wolf wandered back to the fold all on his own."

Void kneels in his own blood, jaw-brand catching starlight. Three wagons gutted. Guards senseless in the ash. Somewhere behind you, someone is still breathing in ragged pulls, alive by luck or stubbornness.

The night is young and you have a branded slaver at your mercy.

The steel finds the soft hollow beneath his jaw. Void does not flinch. Men who have lived by blood develop a peculiar calm when it comes for them at last.

But a voice cuts through the dark before you can lean into it.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"Wait."

She comes from behind the third wagon, a hand pressed to her ribs, moving with the careful deliberateness of the recently clubbed. Dark hair, sharp eyes that have not gone soft despite the blood on her temple. She is not a merchant. The way she moves says soldier, or something close to it.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"He knows why they hit this caravan specifically. Kill him now and that dies with him."

She stops three paces away, studying Void with an expression that is not mercy, only calculation.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"You want to know why Valerius sent his dogs to this particular road on this particular night. So do I."

Void says nothing. His pale eye slides from the blade to the woman and back again. Something moves behind it, cautious and watchful, a man weighing how much his silence is worth and whether he will live long enough to spend it.

The wound in his side is still drinking him dry.

[SAY:Korrag]"The man bleeding in the dirt says you know something. So talk. Who are you, and what's in the box."

Morwen holds your gaze without blinking. She is measuring you the same way you are measuring her, reading the pit-fighter's scars beneath the chainmail, the Northlander breadth of shoulder, the way you carry the sword like a natural limb.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"Morwen. I work for people who want Valerius stopped as badly as you apparently do." She nods at the brand on Void's jaw. "That mark has been turning up on bodies from here to the High Gate. Men with unnatural strength who don't stop when they should. Something he is doing to his fighters changes them."

She reaches beneath her riding coat and produces a flat iron box, dented where someone's cudgel found it.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"This ledger documents every shipment moving through the Gilded Cage. Names, dates, quantities. Not of slaves." Her voice drops. "Of something called the Binding Draught. Whatever it does to a man, Valerius has been manufacturing it in quantity."

She looks at you steadily.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"I need someone who can fight and doesn't frighten easily. The Gilded Cage will kill me before I get three steps inside alone."

[NPC:Morwen Ulvane|wounded, urgent|acquaintance]
[NPC_PRONOUN:Morwen Ulvane|she/her]

[QUEST:The Gilded Cage|offered|Infiltrate the clandestine fighting arena beneath Ashenveil to uncover the source of the Binding Draught and dismantle Valerius's operation.]

[TIME_ADVANCE:10m]

You yank the leather cord from Void's belt with one hand, keeping your boot on his sword arm. He does not resist. The wound has done more to break him than the steel ever could, that slow, patient hemorrhage that whispers louder than any threat.

You wrench his wrists behind his back and cinch the cord until the leather bites deep into the skin. He grunts, more from pride than pain.

[SAY:Void Ironside]"Valerius will send a hundred more," he mutters into the ash. "You know that."

[SAY:Korrag]"Let him."

You haul him upright by the collar and prop him against the wagon wheel like discarded cargo. His pale eye tracks you with something between hatred and a grudging assessment, the look of a man recalculating what he thought he knew.

Morwen watches from the edge of the firelight, her hand still pressed to her ribs. The iron box sits at her feet. Around you the crossroads breathes its cold, ashen silence, broken only by the distant groan of a senseless guard and the creak of jackknifed wagon wood settling in the dark.

The South Road runs straight toward Ashenveil's High Gate. Void is bound and bleeding. The ledger exists.

The next move is yours.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"We take the South Road at first light. Arriving by night draws the wrong eyes."

She glances at Void, slumped against the wheel, his wrists dark with cord-bite.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"What do you want to do with him."

The question carries no sentiment either way. She would leave him for the crows or drag him to a magistrate with equal composure, whatever serves the next step.

The cold wind off the Blighted Reach pushes ash across the crossroads in slow, gray curtains. Somewhere north, beyond the dark tree line, a wolf calls once and receives no answer. The merchant guards breathe in the dirt, unknowing. The dead horse has stopped its terrible noise at last.

Void's pale eye finds you across the dark. Whatever he was before tonight, he is diminished now, a blunt instrument snapped at the hilt. But his warning hangs in the air like the smell of blood.

Valerius would send more.

You leave Void to the ash and the cold. He will live or he will not. Either way he is no longer your problem.

Morwen falls into step beside you without a word, the iron box strapped beneath her coat. You walk through the guttering dark and into the deep quiet of early morning, the South Road hard-packed beneath your boots, the Blighted Reach receding at your backs like a bad dream losing its grip.

By the time Ashenveil rises from the gray, the frost has silvered every stone. The city sits heavy and walled behind its High Gate, a sprawl of merchant houses, cramped alleys, and the particular stench of too many people pressed together behind too much ambition. Guards at the gate wear the livery of no house you recognize, their eyes moving across new arrivals with the flat professional hunger of men paid to notice things.

Morwen leans close as you join the trickle of dawn traders filing through.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"The Gilded Cage sits beneath the Vardenmoor Counting House. Respectable front. Coin-changers above, blood sport below." Her voice is barely breath. "We need a way in. Fighters enter as competitors or cargo. Neither is comfortable."

The gate guard's gaze snags on you. On your size, your scars, the chainmail beneath a traveler's dust. He takes half a step forward.

[SAY:Calenmir Saltborn]"You. Northlander. State your business in Ashenveil."

[NPC_PRONOUN:Calenmir Saltborn|he/him]

But your hands remember what your mind has not yet processed. Back at the crossroads, before the walk south, you crouched in the ash and closed your fingers around one of the abandoned cudgels, a heavy thing of iron-banded oak, still tacky with someone else's blood. You strapped it through your belt beside the longsword and did not think much of it after.

It rides there still, dull and purposeful.

[ITEM_GAINED:Slaver's Cudgel]

The guard clears his throat. The frost smokes faintly between you. Morwen stands half a step back, her expression carefully neutral, the iron box hidden and her hands visible, playing the part of unremarkable traveling companion with practiced ease.

[SAY:Calenmir Saltborn]"I asked you a question, Northlander."

[SAY:Calenmir Saltborn]"Plenty of that in Ashenveil." He steps back half a pace, not warmly, but the blade-hand drops. "Keep your steel sheathed inside the walls. Blood spilled without a writ costs you a hand."

He waves you through with the contempt of a man who has more important things to ignore.

Morwen drifts through behind you without so much as a glance exchanged. Smart. You do not look back.

The main thoroughfare opens ahead, wide cobblestone slick with frost, flanked by the tall facades of counting houses and the lower, meaner faces of taverns wedged between them. The city breathes its coal-thick morning breath all around you.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"Smoothly done," she says quietly, without admiration. Merely acknowledgment.

[SKILL_SUCCESS:Intimidation]
[SUBLOCATION_LEAVE]

Morwen walks a half-step behind your left shoulder, her voice low beneath the noise of the waking city.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"We need to find the Vardenmoor Counting House before the morning crowd thickens. The less time we spend visible on the main street, the better."

Somewhere deeper in the merchant district a bell tolls the hour, iron and flat, swallowed quickly by the stone and smoke. A cart horse clops past hauling barrels that smell of salt fish. Two figures in dark coats watch the gate traffic from a doorway across the street, their faces turned just enough away to seem deliberate about it.

They may be nothing. In Ashenveil, probably everything is nothing.

But one of them has a jaw that sits at a wrong angle, the particular thickness of a man who has taken too many blows in enclosed spaces. A fighter's jaw. And his eyes, when they slide across the crowd, move with professional patience rather than idle curiosity.

He has not looked at you yet.

The place smells of wet wool, rendered fat, and the particular sourness of cheap ale spilled and never fully mopped. A dwarf woman behind the bar watches you enter with the flat professional suspicion of someone who has seen every variety of trouble walk through that door.

Morwen slides in behind you and lets the door fall shut. She moves immediately to the wall beside a shuttered window, angles herself so she can see both the entrance and the street through a gap in the shutter boards.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"You saw them."

Not a question.

[SAY:Korrag]"The one with the broken jaw. Arena work."

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"They were watching the gate, not the street. They're logging arrivals." She keeps her voice beneath the clink of crockery. "Which means someone told them to expect fighters coming in from the north road."

The tallow flames gutter in a draft from somewhere.

[TIME_ADVANCE:10m]

You lean your back against the wall beside her, arms folded, voice dropped to nothing above the ambient clatter of bowls and boots.

[SAY:Korrag]"The two outside. Do I know them from the pits?"

Morwen shakes her head once, precise.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"I was hoping you could tell me. I know faces from ledgers. You know faces from blood."

You think on it. The one with the ruined jaw, broad through the chest, standing with the particular stillness of a man conserving energy between bouts. The second one you only caught a glimpse of, thinner, keeping his chin down. Neither face surfaces from the catalog of men you have stood across from in enclosed spaces. But the posture is unmistakable. Whoever trained them, it was not a soldier's yard.

[DICE:Wisdom check (recognition)|8|failed]

The details slip. A face seen once across a pit in bad torchlight might be anyone now. You cannot place them with certainty.

[SAY:Korrag]"Not from my years. Valerius ran fighters through a dozen different dens."

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"Then they may not know your face either." She tilts her head toward the bar. "We need a room and local information before we move on the Counting House. The barkeep looks like someone who sells both."

Her eyes have not left the shutter gap.

[NPC_PRONOUN:Brindun Pallwick|she/her]

[SAY:Korrag]"I'm looking for work. Fight work. Someone told me the merchant district was the place to ask."

A long silence. She wipes the same spot on the bar she has been wiping since you sat down.

[SAY:Brindun Pallwick]"Men who ask that question in this district," she says finally, voice like gravel in a tin cup, "usually already know where they're going. They just want someone else to say the name first."

She looks at you with the flat patience of a woman who has heard every variety of dangerous question and survived them all.

[DICE:Intimidation check (STR, Power Strike posture, Familiar +1)|17|success]

The cloth stops moving in her hand.

She is not a coward, this one. Her jaw stays set and her eyes hold yours with the stubbornness of a woman who has faced down worse. But her breathing changes, shallow and careful, and her gaze drops once, briefly, to the breadth of your shoulders. She makes the calculation that every sensible person makes when the numbers do not favor them.

[SAY:Brindun Pallwick]"Vardenmoor Counting House." The words come out clipped, like she is biting each one off. "East end of the merchant row, black iron door, no sign above it. You go around back, past the cooper's yard, there's a stair going down. Knock twice, pause, twice again."

She steps back from the bar and puts distance between herself and your knuckles.

[SAY:Brindun Pallwick]"You didn't hear it from me. And whatever happens to you down there, I've never seen your face."

[SKILL_SUCCESS:Intimidation]
[QUEST_STEP:The Gilded Cage|Locate the Vardenmoor Counting House in the merchant district|true]

Morwen has already read the exchange from her position by the shutter. She crosses the room with the quiet economy of someone who has spent years not being noticed, settles onto the stool beside you, and wraps both hands around the untouched ale. She does not look at the barkeep. She looks at you.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"Twice, pause, twice."

She absorbed every word from across the room. Of course she did.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"The watchers outside are still on the gate. They haven't moved this direction." She takes a single measured sip, thinking. "We go in as competitors. You present as a fighter looking for a bout. I go as your handler, someone who manages the coin and the contracts. It's the only entry the ledger confirms they accept without suspicion."

She sets the cup down and meets your eyes directly.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"Once we're inside, I need eyes on their stock of the Draught and whatever records they keep below. You need to look like you belong in a pit." A pause, dry as tinder. "That part should come naturally."

Outside, muffled by timber and frost, the city grinds on. Somewhere in the east end of the merchant row, a black iron door waits.

[TIME_ADVANCE:10m]

You are already in Ashenveil. The Ash and Tallow sits squarely in the merchant district, coal smoke pressing down on the rooftops outside, the frost-slick thoroughfare twenty feet beyond the front door.

Morwen watches you over the rim of her cup.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"The Counting House is east. Cooper's yard is the landmark." She keeps it to a murmur, one eye still on the shutter gap. "Those two watchers are between us and it. We go out the back."

She tilts her chin toward the rear door behind the bar, the one that opens onto the back corridor and the narrow stair above. Brindun has retreated to the far end of the bar and is very deliberately not looking at either of you.

The rear door will put you in whatever runs behind the merchant row, away from the gate and the men with arena eyes. From there, east along the back lanes to the cooper's yard is maybe ten minutes of cold walking through Ashenveil's narrower, meaner arteries.

The front door is faster. The front door also walks you directly past the watchers.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"Your call, Northlander. You're the one they'd recognize."

The hearth pops and spits behind you. One of the gray-bowled drinkers scrapes his stool back and leaves without a word, letting in a blade of cold air before the door swings shut again.

[TIME_ADVANCE:5m]

You keep your voice low, below the scrape of the drinker's stool fading out the door.

[SAY:Korrag]"Cover breaks inside. What then?"

Morwen does not answer immediately. She turns the ale cup in her hands, studying the grain of the bar, and when she looks up her face carries the particular flatness of someone who has already run this calculation and did not enjoy the answer.

[SAY:Morwen Ulvane]"Then we are two uninvited strangers in a room full of men who earn their coin keeping strangers quiet." She sets the cup down. "The Cage runs blood sport for paying crowds. The fighters below are not free men. Anyone who walks in without sanction and starts asking questions becomes cargo."
